transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2026-05-20
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Verdigris Head of Infra), Ethan Ross (Verdigris CTO), Priya Kapoor (Verdigris Security)

Auto-generated Summary:
Verdigris Labs is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment for Redwood inference. Primary concerns: SOC2/ISO compliance, BYOK/KMS integration, SSO/SAML and RBAC, audit logs and retention, EU data residency and egress constraints, and performance cost trade-offs. They requested SOC2 artifacts, a pricing scenario for dedicated capacity, and a technical deep-dive for KMS and VPC options.

Topics:
- Compliance: SOC2 Type II, ISO27001
- Identity: SSO/SAML, SCIM, RBAC
- Encryption: KMS, HSM, BYOK, envelope encryption
- Audit & Logging: retention, export, immutable logs
- Deployment modes: Hosted API, Dedicated, Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Data residency & egress controls

00:00 Sophie: hey everyone thanks for carving out the time, this is Sophie from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, i'll run through goals real quick and then daniel will jump in on the technical bits.
00:22 Maya: hi Sophie, thanks. quick context - Verdigris is a biotech data platform, we process sensitive assay data and PHI-ish metadata, so security/compliance is the gating factor for any vendor. we're looking at options where we can host inference either with you guys in hosted mode or, more likely, dedicated or private, because of data residency.
00:45 Sophie: totally, that's what we want to make sure we cover today. high-level questions for you: where's your primary region (EU or US)? what are your retention policies? who manages keys? and do you have an existing SSO provider?
01:06 Ethan: most workloads are EU first, we have an office in ireland, we've been moving stuff to eu-west-1. retention varies, but for assays we keep raw inputs for 30 days and derived artifacts for 2 years — subject to change after legal review.
01:25 Priya: we use Okta for SSO and SCIM for provisioning. we require SAML for auth and want RBAC that maps to our roles. also we have a strict BYOK requirement for any system that touches raw PHI.
01:42 Daniel: great, thanks. quick note — Redwood supports Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC) installs. For BYOK we have KMS integrations and a bring-your-own-key flow; we also support hardware-backed keys via HSM partners. small caveat, the hosted public API does not allow customer-managed keys today unless you opt for Dedicated or Private.
02:08 Maya: ok that matters. can you explain the difference in audit logging between hosted and dedicated? we need immutable logs and longer retention than 90 days potentially.
02:30 Daniel: yes. hosted has consolidated logs we can stream to customer-owned sinks (S3, BigQuery) with a near-real-time event export, retention is configurable on the export side. Dedicated and Private give you direct access to instance-level logs, audit trails including token-level request traces, and longer on-prem retention policies. the audit export is signed and you can ship to your SIEM.
03:00 Priya: does Redwood provide tamper-evidence for logs? we have compliance wanting chain-of-custody for audit events.
03:15 Daniel: we provide signed log exports and recommend a write-once bucket with object lock for archival; for private deployments you can also integrate with your WORM storage and your HSM for signing. i'll include a diagram in the follow-up.
03:40 Ethan: what about SOC2/ISO artifacts — do you have a Type II report and ISO cert? we need details for the security questionnaire.
03:52 Sophie: yes, we have SOC2 Type II and ISO27001. i can share our audit summary and the control matrix; i'll also include the encryption-specific section.
04:10 Maya: any differences in physical access or supply chain requirements between dedicated and private? our legal cares about managed hosters vs full on-prem.
04:26 Daniel: Dedicated is Redwood-managed hardware in a cloud region with additional tenancy guarantees; Private on-prem is fully customer-controlled infra with our control plane optionally federated. for supply chain, private gives you full control; dedicated is still subject to our provider's hardware chain but we do vendor attestations.
04:50 Sophie: to add, Dedicated has contractual SLAs and stricter isolation than the hosted multi-tenant env, but it is still managed by Redwood. if you need fully air-gapped that's private.
05:10 Priya: about keys — BYOK via KMS, do you support envelope encryption and rotation policies? and can we rotate without downtime?
05:30 Daniel: yes envelope encryption is supported. for Dedicated we integrate with your cloud KMS (AWS KMS, Google, Azure) using a key alias you control; rotations are asynchronous and we support automatic rewraps with near-zero disruption. for Private you can use an on-prem HSM and we support PKCS#11 integrations.
06:05 Maya: what about the crypto logs and key access audit? we need to show who accessed which key and when.
06:18 Daniel: KMS providers already have key access logs; we correlate request IDs to key usage and include that in the audit export. for private deployments you can route key ops through your own HSM audit pipeline. we'll show the mapping in the follow-up.
06:43 Ethan: latency is also a factor — dedicated gives us predictable p99s? we have interactive UX that needs sub-200ms for short prompts.
06:55 Daniel: p99 depends on model choice and batch size but dedicated pools are tuned to give predictable tail latencies; we can provision nodes for lower p99s. hosted may have more variance; private can be tuned best but depends on your infra. we should run a benchmark with your prompt set.
07:23 Priya: on identity -- we need SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning and attribute mapping to RBAC roles. can Redwood map SAML assertions to fine-grained RBAC entitlements?
07:38 Daniel: yes, we support SAML + SCIM and have an RBAC engine that accepts attribute-based mappings. you can create role policies and restrict access to models, routes, and environments.
07:55 Maya: are tokens scoped? we need to ensure service tokens can't access prod data unless explicitly allowed.
08:06 Daniel: tokens are scoped to API keys with route/model permissions; we also have per-token cost/usage tracking and tracing so you can audit token activity.
08:22 Priya: do audit logs capture prompt/response content? that's sensitive, we might want redaction.
:08:33 Daniel: good call — by default audit logs capture metadata only; content is only logged if you enable request-level logging. we support automatic redaction and PII scrubbers and you can opt-in per route.
09:00 Ethan: data residency — can you guarantee no egress from EU? we need to ensure keys and data stay in region.
09:12 Sophie: yes, in Dedicated and Private you can pin regions and restrict egress. hosted has region controls but cross-region fallbacks exist for availability — we can enforce no-cross-region routing via policy for enterprise plans.
09:35 Maya: what's the onboarding process for private? legal will want indemnities and a security runbook.
09:46 Sophie: typically NDA -> SOW -> install window. we'll provide install playbook, runbooks, and a support escalation path. Private installs come with an enterprise support tier.
10:05 Priya: how about backup of model artifacts that contain proprietary model weights — if model weights are customer-provided how do you handle storage encryption and lifecycle?
10:20 Daniel: customer-provided models are stored encrypted at rest using customer keys for Private or Dedicated BYOK if configured. model lifecycle policies control versioning and purge, and we keep full audit trails for model pushes.
10:40 Ethan: what's your retention minimums for logs and how easy to export for e-discovery?
10:52 Daniel: exports can be configured daily to your sink, and retention is policy-driven. we support long-term archival with object lock and can provide signed manifests for e-discovery.
11:10 Maya: anything about regulatory certifications for medical data? do you have HIPAA BAAs?
11:22 Sophie: we have HIPAA-friendly controls and execute BAAs for enterprise customers; will add legal contact. note the BAA often requires dedicated or private deployment for PHI.
11:40 Priya: are there restrictions on model telemetry? some vendors send telemetry to centralized analytics which we can't accept.
11:52 Daniel: telemetry is configurable. you can opt out of telemetry and require local logging only; telemetry is helpful for quality monitoring but can be disabled for private installs.
12:15 Ethan: competitor question — we've looked at AdeptCloud and also thought about building in-house. what are the typical pros/cons from security POV?
12:30 Sophie: AdeptCloud had simpler hosted offerings but limited BYOK; building in-house gives max control but much higher operational burden and slower iteration, risk of missing subtleties around batching, kv cache handling, and cost optimization.
12:58 Maya: ok, can we get an example contract clause around data location and egress? legal will want specific language.
13:10 Sophie: yes we can provide standard data residency clauses and add redlines as needed.
13:25 Priya: what about SSO certificate rotation — if we rotate SAML certs, will auth break?
13:36 Daniel: we support certificate rotation windows and you can upload both old and new certs during rollover to avoid downtime; SCIM is unaffected.
14:00 Maya: audit question — does Redwood provide a single pane of truth for who accessed what across models and environments?
14:12 Daniel: yes the console aggregates token-level traces, per-model usage, and identity mappings; for Dedicated/Private we can also push that to your SIEM for centralized querying.
14:35 Sophie: we've got a couple of asks from this call: share SOC2 artifacts, BYOK playbook, dedicated pricing, and schedule a technical deep dive. is that accurate?
14:48 Ethan: yes, and add a benchmark run on our sample workload.
15:00 Priya: and a short writeup on retention options and WORM/archive recommendations.
15:12 Sophie: noted, we'll put a package together.

(roughly 15:12 mark — conversation moves into more technical Q&A and clarifications)

15:30 Daniel: quick architecture note — for high-throughput low-latency we recommend combining prefix cache and continuous batching; that reduces tokens and cost but it changes KV cache semantics. pardon if i mangle the phrasing the auto-transcript sometimes says key V cache.
15:55 Maya: yeah -- we care about cache isolation per-tenant and ensuring prompt privacy.
16:10 Daniel: we do per-tenant KV cache isolation; in private deployments you can opt for ephemeral caches that are evicted per-request for maximum privacy but with latency trade-offs.
16:32 Priya: do you support encrypted in-memory cache using enclave tech?
16:44 Daniel: not productionized yet; we have roadmap items around TEEs and confidential compute, we'll sofa that into the roadmap and can prioritize if it's a blocker.
17:05 Ethan: about incident response — what's your timeline for notifying customers?
17:18 Sophie: we have an incident SLA: 1 hour for severity-1 notification, full timeline and post-mortem within 72 hours. Dedicated/private customers get a dedicated phone channel.
17:40 Maya: ok SLA is important for us. also we may run a short POC with dedicated for 6 weeks.
17:52 Sophie: that aligns with typical pilots. our POC playbook includes data minimization, a scoped model set, and success criteria we can codify.
18:10 Priya: success criteria: no data egress, BYOK in place, SSO with RBAC configured, and p95 latency < 200ms for our test prompts.
18:25 Daniel: sounds good. i'll run the benchmark and return results.
18:40 Maya: on encryption we need to see key rotation docs and a sample KMS integration manifest for AWS KMS with grant patterns.
19:00 Daniel: i'll include that.

(near the end we recap)

45:00 Sophie: recap — deliver SOC2/ISO artifacts, BYOK playbook, dedicated cost scenarios, benchmark, and schedule the deep technical meeting. Dani el will lead benchmarks, i'll coordinate docs and schedule.
45:30 Ethan: thanks all, good session.
46:00 Priya: we'll send our retention/PII list and legal contact for BAA.
46:30 Sophie: thanks team, we'll follow up.

End of transcript.
